approved: Universities Accord (Cutting Student Debt by 20 Per Cent) Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would cut certain student loan debts by 20 per cent and make the repayment system fairer.
It would reduce debts incurred on or before 1 June 2025 under several student loan schemes, and raise the minimum repayment threshold to $67,000 in 2025-26 with a marginal repayment method.
The debt reduction would affect 3 million Australians, with about 70% of HELP debt repayers aged 35 or younger.
Reduces certain student loan debts by 20 per cent.
Increases the minimum repayment threshold from $54,435 in 2024-25 to $67,000 in 2025-26.
Introduces a marginal repayment system where compulsory repayments apply only to income above the new threshold.

Australians with student loan debts under the Higher Education Support Act 2003, VET Student Loans Act 2016, Australian Apprenticeship Support Loans Act 2014, Student Assistance Act 1973, and Social Security Act 1991.

Universities Accord (Cutting Student Debt by 20 per Cent) Bill 2025 - Third Reading - Pass the bill

Moved the Universities Accord (Cutting Student Debt by 20 Per Cent) Bill, proposing an automatic 20 per cent reduction for three million Australians, a higher repayment threshold, lower minimum repayments and a new marginal repayment system.

Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders to allow extended sitting hours and statements on the Early Childhood Education and Care (Strengthening Regulation of Early Education) Bill 2025 and Universities Accord (Cutting Student Debt by 20 Per Cent) Bill 2025, citing the bills' urgency; the motion was agreed to.

Argued that the Universities Accord (Cutting Student Debt by 20 Per Cent) Bill 2025 provides immediate relief but is poorly targeted, benefits higher earners and leaves non-university Australians behind; the government said it would cut debt for three million Australians and make repayments fairer, and the bill passed its second reading.

Asked how young Australians could repay student debts faster and get ahead; the response described legislation to cut 20 per cent of student debt, remove $16 billion of debt, apply reductions based on 1 June 2025 balances, and changes to lending guidance affecting HELP debt.

Supported the Universities Accord (Cutting Student Debt by 20 Per Cent) Bill 2025, arguing that reducing student debt would improve affordability and generational equality, while later acknowledging concerns that the 20 per cent cut was poorly targeted and could leave some graduates repaying debt for 40 years or more.

Moved a timetable for consideration of the Universities Accord (Cutting Student Debt by 20 Per Cent) Bill 2025, the Early Childhood Education and Care (Strengthening Regulation of Early Education) Bill 2025 and Australia-United Arab Emirates trade bills from Tuesday, 29 July 2025 to Thursday, 31 July 2025, including limits on debate and scheduled votes.

Supported the Universities Accord (Cutting Student Debt by 20 Per Cent) Bill, arguing it would reduce HECS, VET and TAFE debts, lower annual repayments and provide cost-of-living relief, while also citing study hubs, paid placements, fairer indexation and fee-free TAFE as measures to widen education access.

Supported legislation to reduce student debt by 20 per cent, saying it would assist around 21,000 Bonner residents, provide cost-of-living relief, build on free TAFE and preserve the integrity and value of the HELP system.
